analysis: Examined: (1) docs/reference/protocol-messages.md head 1147-1155. GLM no longer refuses `strict` tools, forced `tool_choice` or `response_format` JSON modes. The doc says these are served by post-generation validation: output is withheld until end of stream, validated (ToolConstraintValidation.validate, compileResponseSchema), and rejected with 422 `tool_noncompliance`. Reasoning streams on a separate channel. `reasoning.summary` and `generate_summary` are no-ops; `include_reasoning:false` and `reasoning.exclude:true` are refused. The doc also says tool-constraint v1 is advertised for managed GLM identities, so the coordinator routes forced-choice requests to them. This is a capability and integrity contract change, not a confidentiality change: the provider stays a plaintext endpoint (T-056, T-007). Post-validation does not prove correct computation by an adversarial provider (ADV-001). Integration should verify the cited Swift sources. Specifically: no content is exposed before validation, which matters for 1153's withheld-output and deadline interaction. Also confirm that advertising capability via ToolChoiceEnforcementPolicy.advertisesCapability (head 1154) is limited to managed GLM model types and not caller names (head 1141-1142). These sources are outside this batch. (2) fixtures/prompt-contract/glm53-flash/README.md head 45-48 is a matching doc update. It explicitly disclaims that these vectors qualify those modes. No overclaim found. (3) The libs/mlx-swift-lm submodule moves from 7bed8216 to baca4acf. This is the in-process inference engine inside TB-007, which handles decrypted A-001 and KV/GPU memory (T-028, T-041). The submodule diff is not supplied, so it is unreviewed. This is a coverage limit, not evidence of safety. (4) The new GLM5NextWiredLimit.swift is advisory only; per its doc comment, capacity, admission and KV grants never read it. It reads sysctls and Metal working-set data. It emits fixed sudo sysctl and LaunchDaemon text built only from numeric values and constant labels and paths. The only interpolated string is the local cliName in notice(). It performs no privileged execution itself and has no network input. isMetalOutOfMemory matches error text; callers are not visible. Integration should confirm that callers do not log request content alongside the notice (line ~93 states none) and do not change admission based on it. No concrete regression was identified.
